domain.basis:
Reviewed the complete current 220-line report and its task/effective requirements as a benchmark-design, statistics and deployment-evaluation specialist. No required domain correction found. HELM Classic's 30 models, 16 core scenarios and seven metric categories are distinguished from Lite's reduced seeds/metrics/subjects and Capabilities' five scenarios, zero-shot CoT, changed judges and normalized arithmetic mean. The original Lite and Capabilities documents support the explanation that mean win rate depends on the comparison set and is not interchangeable with the newer mean score. The 0.005 top-score difference is not converted into a deployment success effect. Capabilities' actual dated judge names, Turbo quantization, altered Omni-MATH judge prompt, and inconsistent dated evaluated-model names in its prose versus score table are accurately retained as reproducibility limits.
MMLU-Pro v6 sections 4 and 6/Table 3 support the 19.1 percentage-point GPT-4o prompt difference, five-shot condition with Gemini exceptions, and regex plus random-fallback extraction; these are not equated to HELM's zero-shot adaptation or the current README's optional retry-on-wrong setting. EvalPlus v3 methods, Table 3 and its actual table image confirm the greedy ChatGPT/Phind/Wizard ranking change and all four reported differences. One deterministic greedy completion is kept separate from 200-sample temperature sweeps and pass@k. Stronger tests, contracts and reference corrections demonstrate verifier sensitivity, not universal repository competence.
The Verified 138-task audit is explicitly a difficult selected subset, not an unbiased estimate for all 500 tasks. The July Pro pipeline/human counts and initial filtering are not conflated with later Scale Pro V2's 642 tasks, corrected instructions, restricted network and pristine regrading. Verified and Pro variants are not presented as one time series. The current SWE-bench guide confirms run_id/instance_id result caching can ignore changed patch diffs. Original tau-bench specifies agent temperature 0, user temperature 1, gpt-4-0613 simulator, 30 agent actions and at least three main-result trials; 48.2% is an equal-domain average, while 53.32% is separately labelled arithmetic from rounded domain rates. pass@k and pass^k have the correct complementary existence/all-success meanings, and the homogeneous independent 60% illustration is not an estimate of actual task heterogeneity. tau2's dual-control/user error limitations and the 2.0.0 scoring/input break are retained.
Original Arena, AlpacaEval-LC and configuration documentation support the distinction between self-selected human pairwise preference and fixed-instruction, reference/judge-specific evaluation. The 22.9–64.3 versus 41.9–51.6 verbosity ranges and five-model judge ordering are correctly bounded; p=0.07 is not claimed significant at 0.05. The Leaderboard Illusion simulation is distinguished from measured live effects and Arena's response/provisional-score policy. Oren's permutation argument retains exchangeability and likelihood-access assumptions, not a universal contamination detector. LiveCodeBench's current release_latest is distinguished from pinned release_v6. HELMET's 59-model study and section 3 support diverse task testing without treating needle retrieval as a general long-context proxy. METR's 16 experienced developers/246 randomized familiar-project tasks and 19% slowdown are properly bounded; the later selection and concurrent-time problems prevent a timeless productivity multiplier.
Read the existing worked_calculations.py and all worked-calculations.json results without executing them. Arithmetic agrees for CoT and coding differences, equal-domain/task-weighted tau rates, 97.44% at-least-one versus 12.96% all-four illustration, 1.78885 percentage-point hypothetical binomial SE, and 41.4/9.7-point verbosity ranges. The standard-error example is explicitly hypothetical and paired/cluster uncertainty is discussed. The grounded-support and repository-agent sections require evaluation of the actual retriever/tools/policies/patch/runtime/verification and human correction costs, rather than promoting any benchmark score into an unmeasured product outcome. Historical model service availability and complete hash-pinned runtime/output recovery remain explicit unresolved items; no new service/model run is represented as completed.
